original_question: Are either of the Borel selection classes S1(BOmega,BOmega) or Sfin(BOmega,BOmega) preserved by finite powers?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.3 in §6.2 (Finite powers): "Are any of the classes S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) preserved by finite powers?" ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem targeted in the paper: it names the two correct Borel properties, S1(BΩ, BΩ) and Sfin(BΩ, BΩ), and asks exactly about preservation under finite powers. That matches Problem 6.3 up to very minor phrasing. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient setting is sets of real numbers (equivalently, subspaces of the reals in the chapter’s scope), not arbitrary topological spaces in full generality. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

BΩ must be unpacked: it denotes the family of countable Borel ω-covers of the space in question; likewise B denotes countable Borel covers. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

A cover is taken to be nontrivial, meaning the whole space itself is not a member of the cover. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

An ω-cover means that every finite subset F of the space is contained in some member of the cover. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the selection principles should be stated explicitly: S1(A, B) means selecting one element from each cover in a sequence from A so that the selected family lies in B; Sfin(A, B) means selecting finitely many elements from each cover so that the union of all selections lies in B. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

"Preserved by finite powers" should be made explicit as: for every finite n ≥ 1, the product space X^n (with the product topology) has the same property. This is the intended meaning in §6.2. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

When the property is tested on X^n, the relevant covers are countable Borel ω-covers of X^n itself, taken in the product topology. This is implicit in the paper’s convention that the symbols B, BΩ, and BΓ are collections of covers of the space under discussion. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
refined_question: For a set of reals X, let BΩ(X) denote the family of all countable Borel ω-covers of X, where covers are nontrivial and an ω-cover means that every finite subset of X is contained in some member of the cover. If X satisfies S1(BΩ, BΩ) (respectively, Sfin(BΩ, BΩ))—that is, from each sequence of members of BΩ(X) one can choose one member (respectively, finitely many members) from each cover so that the chosen family is again a countable Borel ω-cover of X—must every finite power X^n, n ≥ 1, with the product topology, satisfy the same property? ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 6.3 in §6.2, so the target is clear. The only refinements needed are to unpack the paper’s standing notation from §1 and §2: the chapter is about sets of reals; S1 and Sfin are the standard selection principles; covers are nontrivial; ω-covers are defined via finite subsets; and in the Borel case B, BΩ, and BΓ denote countable Borel covers, ω-covers, and γ-covers. The sentence immediately following Problem 6.3 adds context by linking a positive answer to the heredity question in Problem 6.1, but it does not give an equivalent reformulation, so no alternate formulation should be supplied. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
